subject: ventures/einvoice-preflight
professional: an e-invoicing integration consultant who certifies ERP output against EN 16931, Peppol BIS 3.0 and XRechnung (KoSIT) validators; first check: does it reject only invoices the official Schematron rejects, and does its arithmetic agree with BR-CO-15/16/17 to the cent

evidence.correctness: Ran checkInvoice (checks.mjs) and the Python port on hand-built invoices and compared with independent computation. Agreed: IBAN mod-97 (DE89370400440532013000, GB82WEST12345698765432, NL91ABNA0417164300 accepted; last-digit mutations rejected INV-025; short DE IBAN rejected INV-024); VAT check digits for DE, FR, NL, AT, ES, IT, BE (known-valid numbers pass, one-digit mutations fail INV-023); SIREN Luhn (732829320, 552120222, La Poste 356000000 valid, 732829321 invalid; my own Luhn agrees); Leitweg-ID MOD 97-10 (I computed the one valid check pair for prefix 04011000-1234512- as 68; the tool accepts exactly that); per-rate VAT BR-CO-17 (3 lines of 0.10 at 5% -> tax 0.02 accepted). DISAGREED: roundHalfUpToCents (checks.mjs:30, linenet.mjs roundCents) is Math.round(x*100 + Number.EPSILON), which does not fix binary representation error. Against exact integer half-up arithmetic over 1,399,993 (net, rate) pairs, 1,399 (0.1%) round the wrong way, e.g. 1.50 net at 19% = 0.285 -> exact 0.29, JS says 0.28. Invoice 1.50 @19% with stated tax 0.29 draws a false INV-018 in JS; the Python CLI (src/einvoice_preflight) returns no findings on the same invoice. Likewise 1 x 1.005 with net 1.01 draws false INV-012/INV-014 and the wrong 1.00 passes. So the browser page and API (the main user path) reject some correct invoices, and the JS/Python parity the README asserts is broken. Because I found a wrong output on the primary path, correctness is 2 despite the many agreements.
evidence.completeness: Checked the README claims that can be exercised: JSON/UBL/CII/Factur-X PDF readers (examples/ contains each, examples.test.mjs runs them), INV-001..INV-035 rules, IBAN/BIC/VAT/period/payment-means/terms/remittance modules (each has a .test.mjs and a .py twin), XRechnung/Peppol/France profiles (profile.mjs exports the rule sets), repair, generate (XRechnung UBL / CII), FatturaPA, FA(3), ZATCA, India INV-01, ~70 country mandate pages with tests, mandate-calendar.ics, llms.txt, robots, sitemap. All the test suites pass. Limits the README itself states honestly and I confirm: Python CLI lacks the profiles and PDF envelope checks; Schematron route needs a build (slimdom/fontoxpath not installed, 50 tests skipped); PDF/A (veraPDF) unrun. No stubs or dead features found in the sample read.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/einvoice-preflight: 1333 tests, 1283 pass, 0 fail, 50 skipped (the Schematron/CIUS tests need `npm i --no-save slimdom fontoxpath`, so the official-rule cross-check was not exercised in this run). Python: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests`: 358 passed, 53 subtests. Mutation 1: checks.mjs INV-021 `dueDate < issueDate` -> `<=`: checks.test.mjs failed (1 fail), caught; reverted. Mutation 2: checks.mjs INV-011 `tax > 100` -> `tax > 101`: the whole 1333-test suite still passed, so the line-tax upper bound is untested at its boundary; reverted (git checkout, tree clean). Also no test covers half-cent rounding on JS (the 0.1% defect above passed every test), and the JS/Python parity is not tested by a shared fixture corpus. Real-file corpora (KoSIT, Peppol, ZUGFeRD) are run by eval/ scripts, not by CI, which is good evidence but not a regression guard.
evidence.craft: Read checks.mjs (full), linenet.mjs, iban.mjs, and skimmed vat.mjs/profile.mjs layout. Positives: small single-purpose modules, rule IDs with message plus fix plus JSON path, defensive input handling (non-object, NaN, wrong types), clear comments recording why (e.g. iban.mjs looksLikeCompleteIban documents a past dead-branch bug). Defects: float rounding as above (should use integer cents or scaled decimals); every rule is written twice (JS and Python) with no generated or shared fixtures, which is how the rounding divergence arose; checkInvoice is a ~300-line function with inline special cases (HUF whole-unit tax, MINIMUM/BASIC WL, negative invoices); the README is 110 KB and reads as a run log, hard for a user to navigate; ~70 near-identical country pages and test files are template output committed as source.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'never uploads the invoice' (page logic is client-side; server.mjs is a separate optional API); 'observation, not the KoSIT validator / not OpenPeppol Schematron' (stated in the XRechnung and Peppol sections, and true); VAT check digits 'from memory of the public descriptions, tested on published examples' (honest, and consistent with my independent checks); Leitweg ISO 7064 verified (agrees); France SIREN Luhn with La Poste exception (agrees). The README discloses what was tested only on hand-made PDFs and what is unrun (veraPDF, Acrobat). VENTURE.yaml stage is `prototype` and all hypotheses are `untested`, consistent with no usage claims. Disclaimer present in index.html and llms.txt. Unbacked: 'the browser page and the CLI report the same rule IDs, messages, and cent-rounded arithmetic' (checks.mjs header) is false for the half-cent cases shown above.
evidence.fitness: Walked a bookkeeper's job: drop examples/ubl-invoice-with-defects.xml style files in, get rule IDs with plain-language fixes and JSON output; CLI and CI use via the Python CLI and the Node server; repair and generate routes exist. The tool is usable for the common job and its stated limits are clear. The false-reject rounding case would send a user chasing a non-error on roughly 1 in 1,000 tax computations, and the official Schematron route is off by default and needs a build, so the 'is it going to pass the network' answer remains approximate.
evidence.domain: Compared with EN 16931 business rules (BR-CO-10, 13, 15, 16, 17), Peppol BIS 3.0 R001/R003/R004/R010/R020, XRechnung BR-DE rules, and the KoSIT/ZUGFeRD/Peppol example corpora (the author ran these and fixed real false positives, per README). Method is what an integration consultant does: a fast structural and arithmetic pre-screen with the official Schematron as the authority, and the author says so. Departures: the arithmetic rounding bug; BR-CO-17 per-rate grouping is implemented correctly; HUF whole-forint tax is a real national practice, handled. A consultant would accept it as a pre-screen but not as a substitute for the official validators, which is also how it is described.

defects.what: roundHalfUpToCents/roundCents use Math.round(abs*100 + Number.EPSILON), which cannot correct binary floating error; 1,399 of 1,399,993 (net, rate) combinations round half-cent ties wrong, e.g. 1.50 net at 19% gives 0.28 not 0.29. A correct invoice draws a false INV-018 (or INV-012/014 for 1 x 1.005) in the browser page and API, while the Python port accepts it.
JS and Python disagree on the same invoice, contradicting the 'same rule IDs, messages and cent-rounded arithmetic' claim; no shared fixture corpus runs both engines.
Mutating the line tax upper bound (tax > 100 to > 101) survives all 1333 JS tests: no boundary test for INV-011.
50 tests (Schematron/CIUS, official-rule cross-check) are skipped unless slimdom and fontoxpath are installed, so a plain `node --test` run does not exercise the authoritative-rule comparison.
README is 110 KB of run-log prose with the user-facing quick start buried; ~70 templated country pages and tests committed as source.

verdict: A broad, honestly caveated e-invoice pre-screen that passes 1283 JS and 358 Python tests and agrees with independent computations of IBAN mod-97, seven countries' VAT check digits, SIREN Luhn, Leitweg MOD 97-10 and per-rate VAT. It does not meet the bar because its core cent-rounding function is wrong on about 0.1% of half-cent ties (1.50 at 19% flagged as an error when 0.29 is right) in the JS engine that serves the page and API, the Python port disagrees, and no test catches it; a seeded boundary mutation on the line tax limit also survived the whole suite. Fix is small: do money arithmetic in integer cents or scaled decimals in roundCents/roundHalfUpToCents and add a JS/Python shared-fixture test. Scores reflect the state before any fix.
